validation_report.joint_verdict_scope: The joint asks a conjunction. Run validity under the contract's own invalidation rules HOLDS. 'Controls satisfied as SPECIFIED rather than as reframed' does NOT hold: the byte-identity control was reframed from a per-cell comparison into an assertion with zero detection power. Nothing about the measured values breaks.

producer_declaration_assessed.why: validity.reason asserts 'byte identity holds on every instance'. Nothing in the run checked that; the assertion is true only because this validation checked it. The same reason omits the matched null, which is unevaluable from the records.

workerB_double_run_incident.consequence: The 'first completed record wins' rule never had to break a tie between two disagreeing measurements. On this data the rule is a no-op with respect to every reported value.

disclosure_gaps: 11 of the 30 duplicated keys are outside workerB: workerA 3 (7 invocations), workerC 1 (2 invocations), 7 spanning workers (heavy / heavy_closure re-attempts, which are by design).

One key superficially resembles nondeterminism and is not: sem_n19_m3_t3_k7_low_B_equ_s20260913001_d0 / f4_trace_msolve has heavy:1 unreached_memory_cap (16 rounds, 6.80 GB) and heavy:3 completed (20 rounds, d_F4_semaev 4), same system_sha256 9ab973072786. heavy/cells/progress.log shows pid 962 ran it at --mem-cap 8.0 and pid 5726 at --mem-cap 13.0. The instrument's VALUE is deterministic; only its COMPLETION is cap-dependent.

byte_identity.question: Does any per-record comparison of the two instruments' input hashes exist, or is equality only asserted?
byte_identity.answer: Only asserted. No comparison with any detection power exists.
byte_identity.mechanism: run_cells.py:92 computes sha = sha256(boolsys.canonical_bytes(system)); line 97 stores it in `base` as system_sha256; lines 120/146/161 pass the SAME variable as input_sha256 into the F4, closure and Macaulay records. One value, six fields. The fields cannot differ, so the contract's 'a mismatch invalidates that cell' can never fire.

a_comparison_that_does_exist.why_it_is_not_the_specified_check: It guards the post-hoc closure re-evaluation rather than cell validity, runs after both instruments, and compares the same two provably-equal fields.

how_it_could_fail_silently.the_instruments_do_not_consume_the_same_: closure and Macaulay receive the in-memory equation list (run_cells.py:138,159) -- identity by reference, stronger than hash equality. msolve receives instances/<id>.ms, a TEXT TRANSLATION by boolsys.write_msolve (run_cells.py:96) with N extra generators v^2+v appended, hashed separately as msolve_input_sha256 and compared to nothing.
concrete_paths: boolsys.py:346 `if not e: continue` SILENTLY DROPS identically-zero equations from the msolve input while the closure still receives them -- the two instruments would then solve systems with different equation counts, invisibly to system_sha256.
boolsys.py:337 mono_str indexes names[j] over range(mask.bit_length()); a mis-shifted mask names wrong variables with no change to the recorded hash.

The field-equation asymmetry itself: msolve gets x^2+x as explicit generators, the closure works in the Boolean ring. The recorded hash covers only the pre-translation core equations and is blind to this by construction.
how_it_could_fail_silently.evidence_not_realised: 0 of 125 chained instances and 0 of 139 retained systems contain an identically-zero equation, so the drop path was never exercised.

validator_supplied_the_missing_compariso.method: Independent parser (no producer code imported) over every retained <id>.ms: variable line -> index map, each polynomial reconstructed as a set of monomial masks, compared against the canonical system.equations in the sibling <id>.json.

artifact_binding_recomputation.method: Re-derived boolsys.canonical_bytes from each retained <id>.json's `system` field and re-hashed.
artifact_binding_recomputation.caveat: The retained file is NOT the canonical bytes -- run_cells.py:93-94 wraps them in {meta, system, system_sha256}. Hashing the file directly mismatches every record (136/136). A later reader must re-canonicalise and nothing in the package says so.

known_false.contract_requirement: A system with a planted linear dependency that forces a degree-2 solution, where both instruments must return 2.
known_false.closure_solutions_source: brute force over 0 free variables (self-contained, NOT taken from F4)
known_false.limitation: 35 degree-1 generators in 35 variables pin the point by the linear part alone, so a verdict of 2 is reachable without any quadratic reasoning. The control does establish that neither instrument mechanically reports 4 from the Macaulay construction's shape, but it is an easy known-false object and it is the only one.

limitations: Scope is J-1 only. No reading is offered of what the measured degrees mean, whether the stated map is right, or whether anything here bears on Assumption 1 or on EV-DREG-008.
Contract invalidation rule 3 (matched null) is unevaluable from the records and is another reviewer's joint.
Code-level findings about run_cells.py, f4_trace.py and summarize.py describe the current bytes, which do not match the declared code_sha256 (D1). Every data-level finding is independent of that.
Git state was not inspected: the task card forbids running any git command, so whether commit f2a88e4eea0d... exists and reaches the declared code was not checked.

The closure and F4 engines were not re-executed (maximum_runs: 0). Reported values were checked for internal consistency and against retained artifacts, not by re-measurement. A blind re-derivation of the degree statistics themselves is a separate joint.
libclosure.so and libgf2ech.so are absent from the tree, so the compiled instrument cannot be hash-verified at all; closure.c and gf2_echelon.c do match their declared hashes.
